blocks.text: Pitt Meadows houses by price band, September 2026

12 houses sold in September against 37 listed. The price band with the most sales was $1,000,001 to $1,250,000, with 7 sold (58% of the month). Among bands with at least ten homes listed, the highest sales ratio was $1,000,001 to $1,250,000 at 41%.

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Bands with nothing listed and nothing sold are left out. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 37 houses listed in Pitt Meadows and 12 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 32%. Month-end counts move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: What is the reported sale price for houses in Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: The September report gave $1,160,000 for houses in Pitt Meadows, against $1,271,500 the month before. The reports give one sale-price figure and do not say whether it is an average or a median, so use it for direction, not as a valuation of your own home.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: The September report showed 41 days on market for houses in Pitt Meadows and a sale-to-list price ratio of 95%, against 32 days the month before.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house to a house in Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: BC's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow more homes on many urban lots, but each municipality sets the details and many lots are excluded. Check the lot's zoning with the municipality before you plan a suite or coach house.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.
